places.name: Sandstone Retreat

heritage.label: Northwest · sandstone
heritage.note: Layered sandstone and shaded clay walls shape a quiet courtyard stay.

places.highlight: Best at first light, when the cliffs shift from rose to copper.
places.goodToKnow: The final approach includes a short unpaved stretch.
description: A stone-and-clay retreat tucked against the sandstone cliffs of AlUla, minutes from the tombs of Hegra and the old mudbrick town. Wake before dawn for the hot-air balloons, spend the heat of the day in the shaded courtyard, and watch the rock glow copper at sunset.

Two can sleep comfortably; a third can take the majlis nook with the extra bedding provided. Check-in is self-service with a lockbox code sent the morning of arrival, and Arabic coffee and dates are waiting on the tray.

reviews.comment: Watched the balloons lift over Hegra with coffee in hand — exactly the reset I needed. The directions for the last stretch of desert track were spot on.
The courtyard is the whole point in the afternoon heat — bring a hat for the walk to the tombs. The retreat itself was spotless and cool inside.
Second stay this year. The majlis nook at sunset, with the rock going copper, is my favourite spot in the whole Kingdom.

places.name: Rawshan Loft

heritage.label: Hejaz · rawshan
heritage.note: Carved wooden screens soften the afternoon sun and frame the lanes of Al-Balad.

places.highlight: The rawshan turns the late-afternoon sun into moving patterns across the room.
places.goodToKnow: Al-Balad stays lively into the evening, so light sleepers may prefer earplugs.
description: A restored coral-stone loft in the heart of historic Al-Balad, behind a carved wooden rawshan window that filters the sea breeze. Step out into lanes of spice shops, old mosques and lantern-lit cafés.
The loft sleeps two under high timber ceilings, with a compact kitchen and a rooftop nook for the call to prayer at dusk. A short walk from the Corniche.

reviews.comment: The rawshan makes the whole room glow in the afternoon. Waking up in the middle of old Jeddah is something else.
Lovely restoration and unbeatable location. The lanes get lively at night — part of the charm, but pack earplugs.

places.name: Cloud-Top Chalet

heritage.label: Asir · Al-Qatt
heritage.note: A hand-painted geometric panel brings Asir’s vivid domestic art onto the mountain terrace.

places.highlight: Clouds gather below the deck while juniper-covered ridges disappear into the mist.
places.goodToKnow: Mountain roads are winding, and fog can reduce visibility.
description: A timber chalet perched in the juniper-forested peaks above Abha, where clouds drift through the valley below by afternoon. Cool year-round, with a stone fireplace for the mountain evenings.
Sleeps four across two rooms, with a wide deck facing the escarpment. Ten minutes from the cable car and the Tuesday market.

reviews.comment: Sat on the deck and watched clouds pour over the ridge. Needed a jacket in July — worth every riyal.
The fireplace is the heart of the place. Road up is winding but fine in any car.

places.name: Palm Farm Bungalow

heritage.label: Eastern oasis · palm
heritage.note: Date palms cast shifting shadows across the veranda and the old irrigation channel.

places.highlight: A shaded veranda opens directly onto the date grove and its narrow water channel.
places.goodToKnow: Bring insect repellent for evenings close to the palms.
description: A quiet bungalow set among the date palms of the Al-Ahsa oasis, the largest in the world. Shade, birdsong and the smell of fresh dates in season, with springs and caves a short drive away.
Sleeps three, with a shaded veranda for tea and a kitchen stocked with local dates and honey. A gentle, green base in the Eastern Province.

reviews.comment: Fell asleep to nothing but wind in the palms. The host left a basket of khlas dates that we finished in a day.
Peaceful and great value. Bring mosquito spray for the evenings by the palms.

places.name: Najdi Mudbrick House

heritage.label: Najd · earth & plaster
heritage.note: Thick earthen walls, triangular vents and gypsum details shape the sheltered courtyard.

places.highlight: Lantern light settles into the courtyard as the earthen walls release the day’s heat.
places.goodToKnow: The thick walls keep the interior naturally cooler than the courtyard.
description: A restored Najdi mudbrick house beside the mud-walled district of At-Turaif in Diriyah, all thick earthen walls, geometric window slits and a shaded inner courtyard. Cool by day, lantern-lit by night.
Sleeps four around a traditional majlis, steps from Bujairi Terrace's restaurants and the old capital's walls. The quietest corner of Riyadh's history.

reviews.comment: Staying inside the mud walls, then walking to dinner at Bujairi — you feel the history and the buzz at once.
The courtyard stays cool even in Riyadh summer. Beautifully restored, generous majlis.

places.name: Coral Coast Cabin

heritage.label: Southern coast · coral
heritage.note: Weathered timber and coral stone sit beside clear shallows at the edge of the Red Sea.

places.highlight: Step from the porch into clear shallows where the reef begins close to shore.
places.goodToKnow: Bring essential supplies from Jazan; shops on the island are limited.
description: A simple cabin on the coral shore of the Farasan Islands in the Red Sea, where the water runs turquoise and the reefs start a few steps from the door. Mornings for snorkelling, evenings for the ferry-quiet dark and a sky full of stars.
Sleeps two, with a shaded porch and kayaks to borrow. Reached by the daily ferry from Jazan — bring what you need, the island is gloriously off-grid.

reviews.comment: Snorkelled straight off the beach at sunrise. The quiet out here is unreal — no signal, no crowds, just reef.
Bring supplies from Jazan before the ferry. Once you're here it's paradise, but the shop is tiny.
